name: Old Mauve
lede: Old Mauve is a dark, dusky purplish red, [[mauve]] gone deep and worn rather than bright, and it shares its exact screen color with a second library name, Wine Dregs.

sections.title: Mauve, darkened
sections.body:
The library records Old Mauve from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, plate 46 I 5, first recorded in 1925 [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 lists classify it as a dark grayish purple, far from the pale pink-violet most people picture when they hear [[mauve]] [1]. At this hex our library also files a second name, Wine Dregs, at an identical value, the way sediment left in a glass darkens past the wine's own color [1].

The nearest distinct neighbor is Dahlia Purple, about 2.7 units away by CIEDE2000, close behind it [[purplish-red|Purplish Red]] and [[gooseberry|Gooseberry]] [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 28, chroma 27, hue 355 degrees, Munsell 7.0RP 2.8/5.4 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in only 10 of 23,781 paintings, 0.04 percent, as photographed [2]. Italy accounts for 4 of the 10, the largest single share by country [2]. No painter here carries it more than once, so no single artist's name stands out [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [2].

questions.q: Old Mauve shares its exact screen color with which other library name?
True or false: Old Mauve looks like the pale pink-violet most people picture when they hear "mauve".

openers: Old Mauve and Wine Dregs are two library names for the exact same dark, dusky color.
